definition: The Demiurge in PKD's exegesis is the divine artisan responsible for our world — distinct from "the Father, Abba, to whom Jesus refers" (CLM_S_353286207b). PKD oscillates: in some passages the demiurge is St. Sophia, who created man "in his image" (CLM_S_aec6d9ece3); in others it is the "evil or sick demiurge, James-James the mad genius creator," ultimately an instrument of good (CLM_S_1bef5afa11).
interpretive_note: PKD's Demiurge is doubled — sometimes Sophia (the wise, ordering creator), sometimes "James-James the mad genius creator," the irrational, oppressive Lord of Darkness (CLM_S_aec6d9ece3, CLM_S_1bef5afa11). Both are distinct from the transcendent Father whom Jesus called Abba (CLM_S_353286207b). PKD reads the Gnostic structure straight: an evil demiurge created our world; the true God is above and beyond it; humanity is "superior to the creator" — the Gnosis Christ taught (CLM_S_d04443fca3). Yet PKD softens this dualism: the demiurge does not "create" in any robust sense but "arranges what's already there into a good pattern" (CLM_S_38f16a0a6f) — and James-James himself is, ultimately, an "instrument of good" (CLM_S_1bef5afa11).
card_description: The ignorant or malevolent creator god of the material world in Gnostic systems; builder of the Black Iron Prison.
